description:
Hello from Earth2Mars team! 🚀

The road to the Moon and Mars begins on Earth. 

TerraTwin is an interactive journey that takes users from iconic destinations such as Shackleton, Jezero, and Gale to some of our planet’s most remarkable landscapes, revealing how deserts, craters, and extreme environments help prepare us for future exploration. Through NASA imagery, terrain data, and field photography, we discover what Earth can teach us about worlds beyond our own.

Because every journey to another world starts beneath our feet...
summary:
TerraTwin is an interactive field atlas that compares Earth’s terrain with the Moon and Mars using measured data. 

Users choose a lunar or Martian target – Shackleton Crater, Malapert Massif, Taurus–Littrow Valley, Jezero Crater or Gale Crater – and explore thirteen Earth analog candidates, from the Atacama Desert and Haughton Crater to the Qaidam Basin, on a satellite map with NASA GIBS imagery, geotagged field photographs and live SRTM terrain statistics (relief, mean slope, roughness). 

A data-science pipeline then samples NASA LRO LOLA (Moon), MGS MOLA (Mars) and Earth elevation models with the same method on the same 500 m grid, so slope, relief and roughness can be compared fairly across worlds, and ranks the Earth sites whose terrain statistics are closest to the chosen target. 

For every site the app states where the analogy breaks down – vacuum, reduced gravity, the thin Martian atmosphere, radiation – and when data are missing it says so instead of inventing numbers. 

The goal is to help mission teams find and characterise less-studied rehearsal sites using open data.
details:
AI-assisted field atlas of Earth analogs for lunar and Martian sites

Key Features

  • 5 planetary targets (Shackleton, Malapert, Taurus–Littrow, Jezero, Gale) and 13 Earth analog candidates
  • Live SRTM terrain statistics for any selected site: elevation, relief, standard deviation, mean slope
  • Cross-world comparison: Earth vs Moon (LOLA) vs Mars (MOLA) on one common grid
  • Ranking of Earth sites by closeness of measured terrain statistics to the chosen target
  • Satellite map (Esri World Imagery, NASA GIBS MODIS Terra for a chosen month), geotagged field photos with author and license
  • Every site documents how it supports mission rehearsal and where the analogy breaks down
  • No invented numbers: unavailable data are reported as unavailable

How it works

  1. Briefing frames the question for a lunar or Martian target.
  2. Explorer: pick a target, then an Earth site (list or search). The map shows Esri and NASA GIBS layers; the site panel shows live SRTM statistics from a 5 × 5 grid at 30 m spacing (Open Topo Data), field photographs (Wikimedia Commons, NASA Image and Video Library fallback) and a Street View link when available.
  3. Terrain comparison panel: slope, relief and roughness of the Earth site next to the selected Moon/Mars target, plus the five Earth sites with the closest statistics.
  4. Field notes: save and share selected sites.
  5. Method: every data source, marked as "used" or "reference only".

Data-science method

Slope depends on the measuring baseline, so Earth, Moon and Mars are sampled identically: a 5 × 5 grid with 500 m spacing around each point (azimuthal equidistant projection, valid at the poles), bilinear interpolation of each DEM, slope from central differences over 1 km.

Sources: LRO LOLA 118 m (Moon), MGS MOLA 463 m (Mars), SRTM/ASTER 30 m (Earth), processed offline with Python (NumPy, SciPy, Rasterio, PyProj).

Absolute elevation is not compared because the three worlds use different zero levels. The ranking is a distance in a three-metric space (slope, relief, roughness): each metric is log-transformed and scaled by its spread across the Earth sites, so no single metric dominates.

The pipeline was tested on synthetic terrain with known slope before use.

Scientific position and limits

The comparison describes terrain geometry of 2 km patches only. It does not measure geology, regolith, gravity, vacuum, atmosphere, radiation, temperature or mission suitability, and it is not a claim that a site is a proven analog. Diviner thermal data, RADARSAT/SAR, Copernicus, ESA and JAXA catalogs are listed in the Method page as future sources and are not ingested yet.

Technology

All source code is available here.

Frontend:

  • TypeScript
  • React
  • Vite
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Leaflet
  • Recharts
  • Framer Motion
  • Wouter
  • TanStack Query

Backend:

  • Express
  • Zod
  • OpenAPI (Orval-generated client)
  • pnpm workspace
  • deployed on Vercel

Offline analysis:

  • Python (NumPy, SciPy, Rasterio, PyProj)

Our approach

  1. Honesty: measured values only, limits stated for every site.
  2. Fair comparison: one method and one baseline for all worlds.
  3. Openness: public NASA and open data, no registration or API keys.
  4. Reproducibility: the analysis script and its README are in the repository.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Claude (Anthropic), Replit, ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot were used for help in coding, debugging, the terrain-statistics script, creating the globe icon and for editing text.
